content: Cutaneous skin tags are small, benign growths that develop on the skin. They are generally harmless and do not pose any significant health risks. The primary symptom of a cutaneous skin tag is the presence of a growth on the skin. These growths are typically small, although some may grow up to half an inch in length. They are often found on the neck, armpits, trunk, body folds, or other areas where skin rubs against skin. Skin tags may have a narrow stalk connecting them to the surface of the skin. They are usually the same color as the surrounding skin, but in some cases, they may appear darker. Cutaneous skin tags are very common and typically appear after midlife. They are benign and noncancerous. These growths protrude from the skin and are often attached by a short, narrow stalk. Skin tags are usually painless and do not grow or change over time. However, they may become irritated due to friction from clothing or other materials. It is believed that skin tags form as a result of skin rubbing against skin, which is why they are commonly found in areas with skin folds. Individuals who are overweight or have diabetes are at a higher risk of developing cutaneous skin tags. The diagnosis of cutaneous skin tags is primarily based on their appearance. In rare cases, a biopsy may be performed to confirm the diagnosis if the skin tag has an unusual appearance. You should contact your healthcare provider if you wish to have a skin tag removed or if the appearance of a skin tag changes. Treatment for cutaneous skin tags is generally not necessary unless they cause irritation or are cosmetically displeasing. Removal options include surgical excision, freezing (cryotherapy), or electrical burning (cautery). Cutaneous skin tags are typically benign and do not cause significant problems. However, they may become irritated or be considered cosmetically unappealing. After removal, skin tags usually do not regrow, and scarring is uncommon. However, new skin tags may develop in other areas of the body. Complications from cutaneous skin tags are rare. Occasionally, they may cause irritation or discomfort. If a skin tag is accidentally cut, it may bleed excessively. Additionally, some individuals may find skin tags cosmetically unsightly.
